A.explanation: Both forces $F$ point down in the same direction, so resultant force is $2F$ down and they do not form a couple.

B.explanation: The two $F$ arrows are not parallel and opposite, so their vector sum is not zero and they do not satisfy the definition of a couple.

C.explanation: One force $F$ is vertical and the other $F$ is horizontal, so the forces are perpendicular rather than parallel and opposite.

D.explanation: The two forces $F$ are equal, parallel and opposite with separated lines of action, so resultant force is zero but resultant moment is $F$ times separation.

hints: Look at each rod and check whether the two arrows labelled $F$ point in the same direction, in opposite directions, or in perpendicular directions.
Recall a couple requires two equal and opposite parallel forces, so the resultant force $F - F = 0$ but the two moments add to give rotation only.
Compare the perpendicular separation of the lines of action: identify which diagram has opposite parallel $F$ forces at opposite ends that both tend to turn the rod the same way.
walkthrough: Recall the rule for a couple: two forces must have equal magnitude $F$, be parallel but opposite in direction, and act along different lines so resultant force is zero with a non-zero resultant moment.
Check diagram A: both $F$ forces act vertically down at the two ends, so they add to $2F$ and cause translation plus rotation, not a couple.
Check diagrams B and C: in B the forces are not parallel and in C one is vertical and one is horizontal, so neither pair can sum to zero with parallel offset lines.
Check the remaining pair: one $F$ acts up at the left end and the other $F$ acts down at the right end, so they are equal, parallel and opposite.
Their vector sum is zero, but both produce a moment in the same rotational sense about any point, giving moment $= F \times$ distance between the forces.
This satisfies the definition of a couple with rotation only and no resultant force. This is option D.
